comparison: Perfect agreement on background claims (C1-C9) about properdin's dual roles. Both evaluations find these claims appropriately supported by citations and provide essential context for the study.

Strong agreement on CL-12 background (C10-C26). OpenEval finds all claims well-supported by citations. Peer reviewers accept the background but emphasize that Aspergillus is used as a model and specific mechanisms during infection remain to be elucidated. Peer review also includes prior findings (C27-C29) not in OpenEval R2.

Both address prior findings (C27-C29) establishing study rationale. OpenEval finds these supported by authors' previous publications. Peer reviewers accept this context and note the current manuscript extends it with novel evidence.

Both address Cp40 blocking experiments (C30-C32). OpenEval finds data clearly support dose-dependent C3 inhibition. Peer reviewers accept these as part of systematic evidence for C3-independent properdin binding, grouping with C33-C35.

Both address CL-12 opsonization enabling properdin binding (C33-C35). OpenEval finds clear experimental support in Figure 2B-C. Peer reviewers accept these as part of systematic evidence demonstrating C3-independent binding.

Perfect agreement on properdin-depleted serum reconstitution experiments (C36-C40). Both evaluations find these provide strong evidence for C3-independent properdin binding and are part of straightforward, sufficient experimental design.

Perfect agreement on C3-depleted serum experiments (C42-C43). Both evaluations find these provide definitive evidence for C3-independent properdin binding and are part of the systematic experimental approach.
Agreement on A. niger confirmation (C44). OpenEval finds this strengthens generalizability. Peer reviewers accept it as supporting evidence within the systematic approach.

Divergence on C. albicans negative result (C45-C46). OpenEval finds this demonstrates specificity of CL-12-properdin interaction. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, noting it shows the effect is not ubiquitous but provides no answers on specific fungal ligands responsible.

Perfect agreement on oligomer-specific binding (C47-C49). Both evaluations find experimental data support that CL-12 specifically recognizes tetrameric properdin, with no concerns raised about these findings.

Perfect agreement on Bb deposition experiments (C50-C53). Both evaluations find these provide functional evidence that CL-12-recruited properdin can direct C3 convertase assembly and demonstrate functional consequences of the interaction.

Significant divergence on main conclusions (C54, C55, C67, C68, C94, C95). OpenEval finds conclusions well-supported by multiple lines of evidence. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, noting direct evidence of sCL-12-properdin interaction is lacking and multiple mechanisms might be responsible; they request more detailed discussion of whether effect is direct or indirect.

Divergence on novel mechanism claims (C94-C95). OpenEval finds these well-supported as main conclusions. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, expressing reservations about mechanistic conclusions and noting the effect might be indirect but at least C3-independent.

Perfect agreement on soluble CL-12 biological context (C56-C62). Both evaluations accept this discussion about soluble scavenger receptors as appropriate context supporting biological plausibility of soluble CL-12 function.

Agreement on properdin not binding directly to fungi (C63-C64). OpenEval finds this supported by experimental data. Peer reviewers accept this as consistent with the overall model showing properdin requires CL-12.
Agreement on prior findings context (C65-C66). OpenEval finds these supported by citations and data. Peer reviewers accept as valid context that the current manuscript extends with novel evidence.

Perfect agreement on membrane-bound vs soluble CL-12 distinction (C69-C76). Both evaluations accept these mechanistic insights without challenge, recognizing this as important conceptual contribution explaining literature contradictions.

Perfect agreement on biological context discussion (C77-C84). Both evaluations accept this as appropriate speculation about biological implications, with OpenEval noting appropriate distinction between established findings and speculation.

Perfect agreement on oligomerization and functional activity (C85-C90). Both evaluations accept the oligomerization data and discussion of oligomer-specific recognition as consistent with experimental findings.

Perfect agreement on leukocyte-derived vs serum properdin speculation (C91-C93). Both evaluations accept this as reasonable speculation about biological significance, with appropriate qualification of speculative nature.

Perfect agreement on methodological details (C96-C98). Both evaluations accept these factual statements about reagents without challenge, recognizing them as important for interpretation and reproducibility.
